questions.question: Which word describes a person who is kind and generous, and wants to help others?
questions.options: benevolent | vulnerable | belligerent | vindictive
questions.explanation: A benevolent person is kind-hearted and generous — like a neighbour who shares food at a festival.

questions.question: The scientist was very careful and checked every detail of her notes twice. Which word best describes her?
questions.options: melancholy | meticulous | impatient | mendacious
questions.explanation: Meticulous means working with great care over every small detail — exactly what she was doing.

questions.question: Which word names a quiet feeling of sadness that lasts a long time?
questions.options: gratitude | melancholy | elation | rhythm
questions.explanation: Melancholy is a gentle, lasting sadness — the opposite of feeling elated.

questions.question: Choose the word that means 'to work together with others towards one shared goal'.
questions.options: demonstrate | collaborate | infuriate | retaliate
questions.explanation: When people collaborate, they join their efforts — like classmates making one poster together.

questions.question: A sports report that unfairly favours one team shows ___.
questions.options: dialogue | bias | ambition | evidence
questions.explanation: Bias is an unfair preference that shapes how someone reports or judges things.

questions.question: Keeping at a difficult task for months without giving up shows ___.
questions.options: melancholy | punctuation | perseverance | animosity
questions.explanation: Perseverance means continuing to work hard even when things are difficult or slow.

questions.question: In the news, a statement that someone says is true but has not yet been proved is called a ___.
questions.options: source | headline | fact | claim
questions.explanation: A claim still needs evidence before we can treat it as a fact.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly?
questions.options: Zane went to the coast last year. | Zane goed to the coast last year. | Zane did went to the coast last year. | Zane go to the coast last year.
questions.correctAnswer: Zane went to the coast last year.
questions.explanation: Go is irregular: its past simple form is went, with no extra did before it.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: I have visited my grandmother yesterday. | I am visit my grandmother yesterday. | I visited my grandmother yesterday. | I visit my grandmother yesterday.
questions.explanation: A finished time word like yesterday takes the past simple, not the present perfect.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a relative clause correctly?
questions.options: The woman what lives next door is a doctor. | The woman she lives next door is a doctor. | The woman which lives next door is a doctor. | The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
questions.correctAnswer: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
questions.explanation: We use who for people in a relative clause: the woman who lives next door.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form of: 'People recycle old clothes.'
questions.options: Old clothes are recycling. | Old clothes are recycled. | Old clothes recycled. | Old clothes is recycled.
questions.explanation: The present passive is formed with are + past participle: old clothes are recycled.

questions.question: The new metro line ___ in 2020.
questions.options: were opened | was opened | is opened | has open
questions.explanation: One line, finished in the past, takes the past passive: was opened.

questions.question: Litter ___ in the recycling bins, not on the trail.
questions.options: must be placed | must be place | must placed | must placing
questions.explanation: A modal passive needs modal + be + past participle: must be placed.

questions.question: Amina said, 'I am watching the news.' Which sentence reports her words correctly?
questions.options: Amina said that she is watching the news. | Amina said that I am watching the news. | Amina said that she watching the news. | Amina said that she was watching the news.
questions.correctAnswer: Amina said that she was watching the news.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, I becomes she and am watching moves back to was watching.

questions.question: ___ you check your sources, you might share false news without knowing it.
questions.options: Both | Either | Whom | Unless
questions.explanation: Unless means 'if you do not' — unless you check your sources, mistakes can slip through.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: The Digital World and Future Innovation

questions.question: While I ___ the documentary, the power went off.
questions.options: am watching | watches | was watching | watched
questions.explanation: The past continuous (was watching) sets the scene for the sudden past simple event.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: The Digital World and Future Innovation

questions.question: ___ of my parents enjoys loud music — they both prefer quiet evenings.
questions.options: Every | Either | Both | Neither
questions.explanation: Neither means 'not one and not the other' — it fits because both parents dislike loud music.

questions.question: Which compound adjective is written correctly?
questions.options: a well known-festival | a wellknown festival | a well-known festival | a known-well festival
questions.explanation: Compound adjectives before a noun join their two words with a hyphen: well-known.

questions.question: Read this: 'Many cities now close their centres to cars on Sundays. Streets fill with cyclists and families, and shopkeepers say they sell more, not less.' What is the main idea?
questions.options: Shopkeepers dislike cyclists. | Car-free Sundays can help both people and shops. | Cities no longer have traffic problems. | Cars are banned in every city.
questions.correctAnswer: Car-free Sundays can help both people and shops.
questions.explanation: The passage shows two benefits — happy streets and better sales — so that is the main idea.

questions.question: Layla checked the weather forecast, packed a waterproof jacket and told a ranger her route before hiking. What can you infer about Layla?
questions.options: She dislikes hiking in the rain. | She set off without any planning. | She prepares carefully for outdoor risks. | She forgot to bring a map.
questions.correctAnswer: She prepares carefully for outdoor risks.
questions.explanation: Every action — forecast, jacket, telling the ranger — shows careful preparation for the outdoors.

questions.question: Which feature is most typical of a persuasive text?
questions.options: Rhetorical questions that push the reader towards a view | A rhyming chorus after every verse | Stage directions for the actors | A list of ingredients in order
questions.correctAnswer: Rhetorical questions that push the reader towards a view
questions.explanation: Persuasive writers use rhetorical questions, strong opinions and evidence to win the reader over.

questions.question: A headline says: 'Miracle snack melts fat overnight!' What should a careful reader do first?
questions.options: Buy the snack straight away | Share it quickly with friends | Look for evidence from a reliable source | Believe it because it is printed
questions.correctAnswer: Look for evidence from a reliable source
questions.explanation: Careful readers test big claims against reliable evidence before believing or sharing them.

questions.question: Which word means 'a way of looking at or thinking about something'?
questions.options: excursion | perspective | instrument | entry
questions.explanation: Your perspective is your point of view — two people can see the same event differently.

questions.question: The mountain path looked safe but was full of loose rocks. Which word describes the path?
questions.options: meager | classical | treacherous | humble
questions.explanation: Treacherous means dangerous even though it seems safe — just like that path.

questions.question: Which word describes a person who is modest and never boasts?
questions.options: geographic | humble | eager | illegal
questions.explanation: A humble person does not brag, even when they have done something wonderful.

questions.question: During the match, the radio ___ described every goal as it happened.
questions.options: commentary | conduction | caravan | script
questions.explanation: A commentary is a spoken description or discussion of an event while it happens.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: She has been training since three years ago. | She has been training for three years ago. | She has been training for three years. | She has been training since three years.
questions.correctAnswer: She has been training for three years.
questions.explanation: We use for with a length of time (for three years) and since with a starting point (since 2023).

questions.question: We wanted to test the invention; ___, the battery was flat.
questions.options: however | who | either | because
questions.explanation: However links two ideas that pull in opposite directions — we wanted to test it, but we could not.

questions.question: Read this: 'A river that looks calm in the morning can burst its banks by evening after heavy rain far upstream.' Why can floods surprise people?
questions.options: Rain far away can change a calm river very quickly. | Floods only happen in the morning. | Calm rivers can never flood. | Rivers never flood in the evening.
questions.correctAnswer: Rain far away can change a calm river very quickly.
questions.explanation: The danger comes from upstream rain people cannot see, so the calm river changes fast.

questions.question: Which of these is an opinion, not a fact?
questions.options: That documentary was the most boring film ever made. | The documentary was released in 2019. | The documentary was filmed in Kenya. | The documentary lasted ninety minutes.
questions.correctAnswer: That documentary was the most boring film ever made.
questions.explanation: Calling a film boring is a personal judgement; the length, year and location can all be checked.

questions.question: Which word names a part of a plant, like pepper, that adds flavour to food?
questions.options: lamb | sandwich | rice | spice
questions.explanation: A spice, such as pepper or cinnamon, comes from a plant and gives food its flavour.

questions.question: Who designs machines, roads, or buildings?
questions.options: an engineer | a laborer | a carpenter | a janitor
questions.explanation: An engineer uses maths and science to design machines, roads and buildings.

questions.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.options: She writes a letter to her friend every week. | She are writing a letter to her friend every week. | She writing a letter to her friend every week. | She write a letter to her friend every week.
questions.correctAnswer: She writes a letter to her friend every week.
questions.explanation: With she we add -s to the verb in the present simple: she writes.

questions.question: Which word means 'to convince someone to do or believe something'?
questions.options: expose | persuade | gallop | encounter
questions.explanation: When you persuade someone, your words convince them to agree or to act.

questions.question: A village far from the city is in a ___ area.
questions.options: local | spacious | rural | urban
questions.explanation: Rural means in the countryside; urban means in a city or town.

questions.question: Sami was reluctant to jump into the cold pool. What does this tell you about Sami?
questions.options: He jumped straight in with a happy shout. | He was the best swimmer at the pool. | He was unsure and did not really want to jump. | He was furious with his friends.
questions.correctAnswer: He was unsure and did not really want to jump.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means not wanting to do something — Sami hesitated at the edge of the pool.
